families.boundary: A policy or standard governs a population; a guide recommends a practice.
families.responsibility: Issue reusable organizational direction, binding criteria, or nonbinding advice.

families.boundary: Roles, steps, checks, branches, and handoffs are the work product.
families.responsibility: Define how recurring work is performed or how a response is routed.

families.boundary: Scope, strategy, resources, sequencing, readiness, and expected evidence are planned.
The content defines a subject or product; detailed test cases and procedures stay in this established family.
families.responsibility: Define needs, requirements, structure, design, interfaces, detailed test definitions, or product information.

families.boundary: The record supports ongoing control; a decision or trade study remains here even when its analysis is complete.
families.responsibility: Maintain current identities, relationships, allocations, states, issues, proposals, or decisions.

families.boundary: Claims are tied to an actual activity, assessed configuration, or recorded event.
families.responsibility: Preserve what was performed, observed, examined, concluded, handed over, or released.

not_for: Establishing mandatory, assessable criteria or compliance obligations, which belong in an internal standard.
Setting organization-wide mandatory direction, decision rights, or exception authorities, which belong in a policy.
Prescribing step-by-step operational execution sequences or recovery commands for a specific service target.
specifications.summary: Nonbinding practitioner recommendations, options, rationales, illustrations, and usage boundaries
specifications.title: Engineering guide
use_when: An author needs to write a reusable, nonbinding engineering guide explaining recommended practices, options, and tradeoffs.
A team wants to document contextual practitioner advice and worked illustrations without establishing mandatory compliance criteria.
A reviewer is checking whether an advisory guide clearly separates recommendations and limits from binding standards or policies.

not_for: Defining recurring workflow steps for baseline and change control, which belong in a configuration management lifecycle process.
Planning project-specific configuration management schedules, tools, and milestones, which belong in a configuration management plan.
Tracking individual controlled items or established baseline snapshots, which belong in configuration registers or baseline records.
specifications.summary: Mandatory direction governing configuration item identity, baselines, changes, and integrity
specifications.title: Configuration management policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs to author organization-wide or project-wide mandatory configuration management directives.
A governance author is defining baseline control rules, change decision rights, and exception handling for controlled items.
A reviewer is verifying that a configuration management policy distinguishes issuing authority, policy ownership, and issuance state.

not_for: Specialized configuration, cybersecurity, engineering, quality, or risk management policies, which have dedicated policy specifications.
Technical or practice criteria requiring detailed assessable checks, which belong in an internal standard.
Nonbinding recommendations, practitioner options, or operational step-by-step procedures.
specifications.summary: High-level mandatory direction for general subjects outside specialized policy domains
specifications.title: General policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs to establish broadly applicable mandatory duties and decision rights for a general subject.
An author is drafting an organizational or project policy outside configuration, cybersecurity, engineering, quality, or risk domains.
A reviewer is checking whether a general policy separates proposed drafts from effective directives and defines real exception authority.

not_for: Planning project-specific threat modeling, security controls, and assessments, which belong in a security engineering plan.
Preparing incident response governance and escalation workflows, which belong in an incident response plan or playbook.
Recording actual vulnerability cases, security advisories, or selected control implementations.
specifications.summary: Mandatory security direction covering protection objectives, secure development, incidents, and supply chain
specifications.title: Cybersecurity policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs mandatory cybersecurity directives governing protection objectives, secure development, and supply-chain security.
A security governance author is defining security accountability, incident escalation rules, and security exception authorities.
A reviewer is assessing whether a cybersecurity policy separates high-level mandatory obligations from technical implementation plans.

not_for: Defining recurring cross-discipline workflows or handoffs, which belong in systems or software engineering lifecycle processes.
Planning one project's engineering tailoring, resources, and gates, which belong in a systems engineering management plan.
Setting granular technical artifact rules, which belong in an internal standard.
specifications.summary: Mandatory engineering direction for lifecycle duties, requirements, interfaces, and technical decisions
specifications.title: Engineering policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs broad mandatory engineering obligations covering lifecycle duties, requirements, interfaces, and technical decisions.
An author is defining organizational engineering decision rights, coordination rules, and nonconformance escalation routes.
A reviewer is checking whether an engineering policy stays at mandatory governance level without embedding detailed lifecycle procedures.

not_for: Planning project-specific quality objectives, assurance checks, and measures, which belong in a project or product quality plan.
Tracking individual observed defects or nonconformances through closure, which belong in a problem or defect report.
Recording actual verification or audit outcomes, which belong in evidence records.
specifications.summary: Mandatory direction for product or service quality, impartial assurance, and nonconforming outputs
specifications.title: Quality policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs organization-wide or project-wide mandatory direction for product or service quality.
A governance author is defining impartial assurance independence and nonconforming-output control duties.
A reviewer is verifying that a quality policy establishes real disposition authority and review cadence.

not_for: Tracking active project or operational risks, ratings, and treatments, which belong in a risk register.
Analyzing physical or system safety hazards and mishap controls, which belong in a hazard log or safety assurance plan.
Recording already realized defects or active operational incidents.
specifications.summary: Mandatory direction governing risk criteria, ownership, treatment, acceptance, and review
specifications.title: Risk management policy
use_when: An issuing authority needs common mandatory risk management rules across an organization, project, or service boundary.
A governance author is specifying risk criteria, escalation thresholds, ownership rules, and residual-risk acceptance authority.
A reviewer is checking whether a risk policy clearly separates risk identification from authorized risk acceptance.

not_for: Broad organizational duties and decision rights without granular assessable criteria, which belong in a policy.
Nonbinding practitioner advice, options, or style recommendations, which belong in an engineering guide.
Project-specific product or software requirements, which belong in requirements specifications.
specifications.summary: Authorized mandatory assessable criteria and assessment bases for a practice or artifact
specifications.title: Internal standard
use_when: An identified authority needs to publish binding, assessable technical or practice criteria for engineering, security, operations, data, testing, or documentation.
An author is translating domain conventions into verifiable requirements with explicit assessment bases and exception rules.
A reviewer is verifying that an internal standard states unambiguous mandatory criteria distinct from advisory prose.

not_for: High-level mandatory configuration management direction and authority, which belong in a configuration management policy.
Project-specific schedules, tools, and milestones for one effort, which belong in a configuration management plan.
Maintaining live item entries or baseline snapshots, which belong in registers or baseline evidence records.
specifications.summary: Reusable recurring process for configuration item, baseline, change, status, and integrity controls
specifications.title: Configuration management lifecycle process
use_when: An organization needs a reusable configuration management process governing items, baselines, changes, and audits across multiple projects.
A process author is defining recurring configuration state transitions, discrepancy handling, and tailoring rules.
A reviewer is checking whether a configuration management process clearly separates recurring workflow rules from project-specific plans.

not_for: Planning one project's software increments, schedule, and team assignments, which belong in a software development plan.
Cross-discipline hardware, human, and system-wide coordination, which belongs in a systems engineering lifecycle process.
Executing a single service maintenance task or operator recovery sequence, which belongs in a runbook.
specifications.summary: Reusable software workflow spanning development, integration, assurance, control, release, and maintenance
specifications.title: Software engineering lifecycle process
use_when: An organization needs common software lifecycle rules guiding development, integration, assurance, release, and maintenance across projects.
A process author is specifying recurring software work paths, work-product expectations, decision gates, and handoff boundaries.
A reviewer is verifying that a software lifecycle process defines tailoring rules and assurance interfaces cleanly.

not_for: Tailoring systems engineering roles, schedules, and gates for one specific project, which belongs in a systems engineering management plan.
Software-only development and release workflows, which belong in a software engineering lifecycle process.
Recording actual technical review outcomes or transition evidence.
specifications.summary: Reusable cross-discipline process from needs through requirements, architecture, integration, assessment, and transition
specifications.title: Systems engineering lifecycle process
use_when: An organization needs a reusable cross-discipline systems engineering process covering needs through transition and technical gates.
A process engineer is defining recurring technical activities, requirement and architecture controls, and review interfaces.
A reviewer is checking whether a systems engineering process distinguishes recurring lifecycle coordination from project-specific tailoring.

not_for: Planning verification or validation scope, resources, and scenarios for one bounded project, which belong in V&V plans.
Defining step-by-step execution methods for one check, which belong in verification or validation procedures.
Recording actual observed conformance or fitness outcomes, which belong in verification or validation evidence records.
specifications.summary: Reusable V&V process separating conformance and fitness methods, independence, evidence, and anomalies
specifications.title: Verification and validation lifecycle process
use_when: An organization needs a recurring V&V process with shared rules for methods, independence, evidence, traceability, and reporting.
A process author is establishing clear structural separation between technical verification paths and intended-use validation paths.
A reviewer is assessing whether a V&V process defines rigorous result-classification and anomaly-routing controls.

not_for: Pre-incident organizational preparedness, severity taxonomy, and exercise governance, which belong in a cybersecurity incident response plan.
Ordinary vulnerability intake and remediation without suspected exploitation, which belong in a vulnerability response playbook.
Contemporaneous incident logging or retrospective incident analysis, which belong in incident records or post-incident reviews.
specifications.summary: Branching cybersecurity incident response for triage, containment, evidence, recovery, and notification
specifications.title: Cybersecurity incident response playbook
use_when: A security team needs a branching playbook for suspected or confirmed cybersecurity incidents requiring coordinated triage and containment.
An author is defining incident declaration thresholds, evidence preservation duties, disruptive-action approvals, and recovery gates.
A reviewer is verifying that a cybersecurity playbook covers notification decisions and deactivation criteria without inventing authority.

not_for: Suspected or confirmed cybersecurity incidents, which belong in a cybersecurity incident response playbook.
Vulnerability intake, assessment, and remediation tracking, which belong in a vulnerability response playbook.
Linear, unbranched service operations on one target, which belong in an operational runbook.
specifications.summary: Branching operational or business response coordination excluding cybersecurity and unbranched tasks
specifications.title: Generic response playbook
use_when: A team needs a coordinated branching response for an evolving operational or business disruption outside cybersecurity.
An author is defining activation conditions, explicit decision points, authority checks, and stabilization handoffs.
A reviewer is checking whether a generic playbook defines bounded response paths and clear escalation or halt criteria.

not_for: Active containment and eradication of suspected or confirmed exploitation, which belong in a cybersecurity incident response playbook.
Tracking the state of one individual vulnerability case, which belongs in a vulnerability record.
Communicating affected versions and fixes to external customers, which belongs in a recipient security advisory.
specifications.summary: Vulnerability intake, applicability assessment, prioritization, treatment, verification, and disposition workflow
specifications.title: Vulnerability response playbook
use_when: A security or operations team needs a coordinated workflow for handling vulnerability reports, advisories, and scanner findings.
An author is defining applicability checks, priority decisions, treatment branches, and exploitation escalation triggers.
A reviewer is checking whether a vulnerability playbook separates remediation verification from residual-risk acceptance.

not_for: Executing manual step-by-step operational procedures on a live service without a provisioning codebase, which belong in a runbook.
Designing network topology or runtime environment specifications before provisioning code exists.
Recording actual executed deployment runs or release attempts, which belong in execution or release records.
specifications.summary: Governance controls around provisioning code covering source, targets, gates, drift, and teardown
specifications.title: Provisioning governance companion
use_when: A team manages infrastructure with versioned provisioning code and needs a human-readable governance companion for targets, gates, and drift.
An author is documenting deployment authorization, secret boundaries, verification checks, and teardown rules around provisioning artifacts.
A reviewer is verifying that a provisioning companion binds to authoritative code without copying executable configuration.

not_for: Multi-role organizational workflows spanning a broad class of recurring work, which belong in a standard operating procedure.
Highly branching responses to evolving disruptions or incidents, which belong in a response playbook.
Recording actual observations and outcomes of a performed run, which belong in an operational work execution record.
specifications.summary: Ordered operational steps, preflight checks, expected observations, and rollback for one target
specifications.title: Operational runbook
use_when: Operators need an ordered, repeatable procedure with preflight checks, expected observations, and rollback steps for a specific service or system.
An author is documenting a maintenance, troubleshooting, or operational recovery task bound to an explicit target selector.
A reviewer is checking whether a runbook prevents wrong-target execution, unbounded retries, or unverified recovery claims.

not_for: Target-specific service commands, expected system observations, and rollback paths, which belong in an operational runbook.
Fine-grained technique, tooling, and tolerances for one single workstation task, which belong in a work instruction.
High-level lifecycle governance across multiple disciplines, which belongs in a lifecycle process.
specifications.summary: Recurring work procedure defining roles, inputs, decisions, holds, handoffs, and records
specifications.title: Standard operating procedure
use_when: A recurring organizational or operational class of work needs standardized roles, readiness inputs, decision holds, and handoff rules.
An author is documenting a repeatable multi-step process with abnormal routing and required completion records.
A reviewer is verifying that a procedure clearly defines triggers, decision authority, and abnormal-work escalation.

not_for: Coordinating broader cross-role recurring workflows and organizational handoffs, which belong in a standard operating procedure.
Service-level troubleshooting and rollback operations on live infrastructure, which belong in an operational runbook.
Recording actual execution evidence of a completed task, which belongs in an operational work execution record.
specifications.summary: Detailed technique, tools, checks, tolerances, and acceptance criteria for one repeatable task
specifications.title: Work instruction
use_when: A qualified worker needs exact technique, tools, tolerances, checks, and acceptance criteria for one repeatable task.
An author is writing station-level or task-level instructions nested under a broader procedure or work order.
A reviewer is checking whether a work instruction specifies competence prerequisites, check points, and nonconforming-work routing.

not_for: Planning post-delivery software fixes, enhancements, regression testing, and releases, which belong in a software maintenance plan.
Planning decommissioning, disposal, or withdrawal of an asset, which belongs in a retirement and disposal plan.
Recording an actual maintenance action performed on an asset, which belongs in an operational work execution record.
specifications.summary: Plan upkeep, triggers, logistics, work controls, and return-to-service criteria for non-software assets
specifications.title: System, product, or asset maintenance plan
use_when: An owner needs to plan maintenance strategies, triggers, spares, and return-to-service criteria for physical, infrastructure, or system assets.
A planner is defining work controls and assessment gates before recurring servicing or repair begins.
A reviewer is checking whether an asset maintenance plan separates asset upkeep from software change management.

not_for: Broad day-to-day staffing, support, and routine operations models, which belong in an operations and support plan.
Enterprise-wide disruption workarounds spanning sites and business units, which belong in a business continuity plan.
Reporting actual observed availability metrics for a past period, which belongs in a service-period status report.
specifications.summary: Plan availability objectives, measurement rules, failure analysis, resilience provisions, and degradation handling
specifications.title: Service or system availability plan
use_when: A service or system needs explicit availability objectives, measurement rules, dependency failure analysis, and resilience provisions.
An architect or reliability engineer is planning degraded-operation behaviors and monitoring thresholds before sustained operation.
A reviewer is verifying that availability targets align with concrete measurement methods and realistic failure scenarios.

not_for: Technical recovery and failover for one classified information system, which belongs in an information-system contingency plan.
Routine service monitoring and reliability engineering, which belong in operations or availability plans.
Cybersecurity incident triage and containment preparedness, which belong in a cybersecurity incident response plan.
specifications.summary: Plan prioritized business continuity across people, sites, suppliers, restoration, and exercises
specifications.title: Business continuity plan
use_when: An organization needs to prioritize critical business or service capabilities and plan workarounds across people, sites, and suppliers.
A continuity planner is defining activation authority, recovery objectives, communication routes, and return-to-normal criteria.
A reviewer is checking whether a business continuity plan covers exercise evaluation and realistic supplier dependencies.

not_for: Setting organization-wide mandatory configuration direction, which belongs in a configuration management policy.
Defining a reusable cross-project workflow without project schedules, which belongs in a configuration management lifecycle process.
Listing live controlled items or recording an established baseline snapshot, which belong in control registers or baseline records.
specifications.summary: Project-specific configuration identification, baselining, change control, audits, and retention plan
specifications.title: Configuration management plan
use_when: A project needs to assign configuration management responsibilities, tools, baseline milestones, and supplier rules for a bounded scope.
A configuration lead is planning item classes, change routes, integrity checks, and retention timing before project execution.
A reviewer is checking whether project configuration authority and baseline release criteria are concretely defined.

not_for: Branching tactical execution during an active incident, which belongs in a cybersecurity incident response playbook.
Managing ordinary vulnerabilities before suspected exploitation, which belongs in a vulnerability response playbook.
Logging an active incident or reviewing a past incident, which belong in incident records or post-incident reviews.
specifications.summary: Pre-incident cybersecurity governance, severity, escalation, evidence rules, recovery interfaces, and exercises
specifications.title: Cybersecurity incident response plan
use_when: An organization or service boundary needs pre-incident cybersecurity governance, roles, severity levels, and escalation rules.
A security lead is defining evidence-handling standards, communication interfaces, and exercise schedules before an incident occurs.
A reviewer is checking whether incident declaration authority and continuity handoffs are established cleanly.

not_for: Planning cutover, migration, and handover into a live operating environment, which belongs in a transition and deployment plan.
Planning a broader test campaign across all test levels, which belongs in a test plan.
Controlling agreed interface parameters between parties, which belongs in an interface control document.
specifications.summary: Plan staged assembly, interface bring-up, readiness gates, checks, and failure handling
specifications.title: Integration plan
use_when: A project must coordinate staged assembly and interface bring-up across multiple components, subsystems, or software increments.
An integration lead is specifying per-stage prerequisites, support environments, readiness gates, and safe stop criteria before integration starts.
A reviewer is verifying that component configurations and failure responses are explicitly planned across integration boundaries.

not_for: Low-impact or moderate-impact classified information systems, which use dedicated lower-tier contingency plan specifications.
Organization-wide business workarounds across people, facilities, and business processes, which belong in a business continuity plan.
Step-by-step single-operation technical procedures for routine administration, which belong in an operational runbook.
specifications.summary: High-impact system contingency covering failover, data integrity, offsite/alternate dispositions, and optional concurrent processing
specifications.title: High-impact information-system contingency plan
use_when: A responsible authority has classified an information system as high impact and requires a system-specific contingency and failover plan.
A recovery planner is documenting offsite storage, alternate processing, data reconciliation, and optional concurrent processing.
A reviewer is checking whether reconstitution checks, authority limits, and exercise schedules satisfy high-impact recovery objectives.

not_for: Moderate-impact or high-impact classified systems requiring mandatory offsite/alternate dispositions or concurrent processing.
Enterprise business process continuity across non-IT operations, which belongs in a business continuity plan.
Routine preventive hardware servicing or software patching plans.
specifications.summary: Low-impact system contingency for activation, bounded recovery, reconstitution, exercises, and upkeep
specifications.title: Low-impact information-system contingency plan
use_when: A responsible authority has classified an information system as low impact and requires a proportionate system-specific contingency plan.
A system owner is planning activation rules, bounded recovery steps, reconstitution checks, and plan upkeep without heavy failover overhead.
A reviewer is verifying that recovery objectives and optional alternate-storage choices match the system's low-impact classification.

not_for: High-impact systems needing failover reconciliation or concurrent processing, or low-impact systems needing lighter arrangements.
Organization-wide business continuity across people, sites, and manual business workarounds.
Active cybersecurity incident containment and eradication workflows.
specifications.summary: Moderate-impact system contingency with offsite storage and alternate processing, excluding concurrent processing
specifications.title: Moderate-impact information-system contingency plan
use_when: A responsible authority has classified an information system as moderate impact and requires a coordinated system contingency plan.
A contingency coordinator is documenting explicit offsite storage and alternate processing dispositions with prioritized service restoration.
A reviewer is checking whether dependencies, escalation rules, and reconstitution criteria match moderate-impact obligations.

not_for: Detailed command sequences and rollback steps for one operational task, which belong in an operational runbook.
Staged cutover and migration into operations, which belongs in a transition and deployment plan.
Summarizing actual past service-period metrics and incidents, which belongs in a service-period status report.
specifications.summary: Plan sustained service ownership, support, observability, capacity, data protection, and escalation interfaces
specifications.title: Operations and support plan
use_when: A service or system needs a coordinated operating, monitoring, support, and escalation model before or during sustained use.
A service owner is defining support commitments, data protection routines, and operational handoffs across teams and suppliers.
A reviewer is verifying that routine maintenance, change control, and continuity interfaces are aligned for ongoing service operation.

not_for: Maintaining an ordered inventory of emergent work items and refinement states, which belongs in an ordered product backlog.
Detailed engineering delivery schedules or periodic progress tracking, which belong in development plans or status reports.
Binding commercial offers or executed contractual delivery commitments.
specifications.summary: Outcome-oriented product direction, themes, dependencies, and forecast boundaries across planning horizons
specifications.title: Product roadmap
use_when: Product and engineering leaders need to communicate evolving product direction, themes, and intended outcomes across multiple horizons.
An author is documenting strategic dependencies and feasibility assumptions while clearly separating forecasts from commitments.
A reviewer is checking that a product roadmap avoids claiming unachieved outcomes or duplicating backlog execution details.

not_for: Organization-wide mandatory quality direction and independence principles, which belong in a quality policy.
Detailed technical test strategy and case coverage planning, which belong in a test plan or verification plan.
Recording actual audit findings or individual defect closures, which belong in audit reports or defect reports.
specifications.summary: Plan project or product quality objectives, assurance checks, measures, and nonconformity routes
specifications.title: Project or product quality plan
use_when: A bounded project, product, service, or contract requires a coordinated quality assurance approach across its lifecycle.
A quality lead is specifying quality objectives, planned checks, measures, and nonconforming-output routing before delivery.
A reviewer is verifying that planned quality checks map cleanly to an established quality basis and real disposition authority.

not_for: Introducing a replacement capability into live operations, which belongs in a transition and deployment plan.
Ongoing upkeep and routine servicing of an active asset or software product.
Recording actual completed decommissioning actions, which belongs in operational execution or handoff records.
specifications.summary: Plan controlled withdrawal, dependencies, data and access disposition, asset closure, and verification gates
specifications.title: Retirement and disposal plan
use_when: An existing system, service, product, or asset is slated for decommissioning, transfer, reuse, disposal, or end-of-support withdrawal.
A planner is coordinating data retention, access revocation, supplier contract closure, and dependent-service continuity during retirement.
A reviewer is checking whether withdrawal gates and closure verification criteria cover all continuing legal or operational obligations.

not_for: Tracking individual active system hazards, controls, and closure status over time, which belongs in a hazard log.
Analyzing reliability or non-safety failure priorities alone, which belongs in failure modes and effects analysis.
Planning technical cybersecurity protections and vulnerability workflows, which belong in a security engineering plan.
specifications.summary: Plan safety hazard analysis, controls, assurance evidence, safety gates, and lifecycle reassessment
specifications.title: Safety assurance plan
use_when: Established requirements, agreements, or project decisions impose a safety obligation requiring coordinated hazard analysis and assurance.
A safety lead is planning hazard identification, safety controls, assurance evidence, and safety decision gates across the lifecycle.
A reviewer is checking whether safety arguments, residual-exposure authority, and lifecycle reassessment triggers are planned cleanly.

not_for: High-level organizational cybersecurity mandates and escalation rules, which belong in a cybersecurity policy.
Pre-incident detection, severity, and crisis coordination, which belong in a cybersecurity incident response plan.
Recording implemented control claims or individual vulnerability cases, which belong in control records.
specifications.summary: Plan technical protection objectives, threat analysis, secure design, security assessments, and handoff
specifications.title: Security engineering plan
use_when: A project has an established technical security-engineering responsibility requiring coordinated threat analysis, design controls, and assessments.
A security engineer is planning security requirements work, assurance activities, vulnerability routing, and operational security handoff.
A reviewer is checking whether planned security assessments and authorization interfaces trace back to real protection objectives.

not_for: Defining an organization's reusable cross-project workflow without project specifics, which belongs in a systems engineering lifecycle process.
Planning software-only delivery increments and build infrastructure, which belongs in a software development plan.
Recording actual outcomes of held technical reviews, which belong in design review evidence records.
specifications.summary: Project-level systems engineering tailoring, authority, cross-discipline interfaces, resources, and technical gates
specifications.title: Systems engineering management plan
use_when: A bounded project needs a master technical management plan tailoring systems engineering processes, authority, resources, and review gates.
A systems engineering lead is coordinating multiple technical disciplines, suppliers, specialty engineering, and lifecycle handoffs.
A reviewer is checking whether project tailoring decisions, technical interfaces, and gate evidence expectations are coherent.

not_for: Reusable organization-wide software lifecycle rules, which belong in a software engineering lifecycle process.
Post-delivery bug fixes, enhancements, and end-of-support coordination, which belong in a software maintenance plan.
Detailed software architecture, module design, or requirements specifications.
specifications.summary: Plan software increments, environments, secure builds, third-party controls, gates, and release handoff
specifications.title: Software development plan
use_when: A software delivery effort needs a coordinated plan covering increments, development environments, secure builds, gates, and support handoff.
A software lead is assigning responsibilities, third-party obligations, and release readiness criteria across a defined project.
A reviewer is verifying that development controls, assessment gates, and change responses match project delivery obligations.

not_for: Initial development and pre-delivery software increments, which belong in a software development plan.
Physical or infrastructure hardware upkeep and servicing, which belong in an asset maintenance plan.
Full decommissioning and disposal execution, which belongs in a retirement and disposal plan.
specifications.summary: Plan post-delivery software intake, controlled modification, regression assessment, re-release, and end-of-support
specifications.title: Software maintenance plan
use_when: A delivered software item requires a structured strategy for ongoing support, defect fixes, enhancements, regression testing, and re-release.
A maintainer is defining intake triage, change authorization, support commitments, and end-of-support migration routes.
A reviewer is checking whether post-delivery software modification workflows align with release and operational dependencies.

not_for: Negotiating commercial offers or documenting executed contract terms, which belong in proposals or contracted work agreements.
Managing internal software development without supplier acquisition oversight.
Recording actual acceptance decisions or formal transfer receipts, which belong in evidence records.
specifications.summary: Plan supplier evaluation, requirement flow-down, oversight, delivery assessment, and receiving criteria
specifications.title: Supplier assurance plan
use_when: An acquirer needs coordinated technical oversight, deliverable flow-down, and receiving criteria for supplied items or services.
A supplier manager is planning due diligence, oversight checkpoints, issue escalation, and acceptance routes under an actual agreement.
A reviewer is checking whether supplier assurance activities stay strictly bounded by established oversight rights.

not_for: Deriving detailed test conditions, cases, or step-by-step execution scripts, which belong in test design, case, and procedure specifications.
Planning broader multi-method verification or intended-use validation programs beyond testing, which belong in V&V plans.
Reporting mid-campaign progress or ended-campaign outcomes, which belong in test status or test completion reports.
specifications.summary: Plan test scope, basis, strategy, resources, gate criteria, and evidence before execution
specifications.title: Test plan
use_when: A test campaign, test level, or release requires an agreed scope, strategy, schedule, resources, and gate criteria before testing starts.
A test lead is aligning stakeholders on test basis coverage, environment dependencies, and evidence expectations.
A reviewer is verifying that entry, exit, suspension, and resumption criteria are observable and assigned to real decision authorities.

not_for: Assembling components and bringing up interfaces before operational entry, which belongs in an integration plan.
Withdrawing or disposing of an obsolete capability, which belongs in a retirement and disposal plan.
Recording actual release events or completed responsibility transfers, which belong in release or handoff records.
specifications.summary: Plan readiness, cutover sequence, recovery, operational checks, handover, and stabilization into service
specifications.title: Transition and deployment plan
use_when: A capability is entering live operations through deployment, migration, cutover, or service transfer and needs coordinated readiness planning.
A transition lead is sequencing cutover stages, stop and reversal conditions, operational checks, and stabilization handover.
A reviewer is verifying that receiving-environment readiness, data migration controls, and rollback limits are explicitly planned.

not_for: Participant-facing notices explaining study arrangements prior to consent, which belong in research participant information.
Exact interview prompts or questionnaires, which belong in an elicitation instrument specification.
Reporting completed research observations or assessing fitness of an established solution, which belong in research findings or validation plans.
specifications.summary: Plan exploratory user discovery questions, recruitment, methods, ethics, rounds, and analysis
specifications.title: User research and discovery plan
use_when: A team faces unknown user needs, workflows, or operating contexts and needs a structured exploratory research plan.
A researcher is planning sampling criteria, collection methods, privacy safeguards, and round readiness before engaging participants.
A reviewer is checking whether a discovery plan addresses ethics, data handling, and interpretation limits before collection.

not_for: Planning verification alone or validation alone as separate packages, which use dedicated verification or validation plan specifications.
Planning a single software testing campaign without broader inspection, analysis, or demonstration paths, which belongs in a test plan.
Defining reusable cross-project V&V workflows, which belong in a V&V lifecycle process.
specifications.summary: Coordinate verification and validation in one plan with distinct bases, mappings, and criteria
specifications.title: Combined verification and validation plan
use_when: One project needs a unified plan coordinating both technical verification and intended-use validation under a single program scope.
A V&V lead is mapping both technical obligations and stakeholder needs while keeping criteria, bases, and conclusions distinct.
A reviewer is checking that shared events preserve separate pass criteria for verification versus validation.

not_for: Assessing conformity to specified technical requirements, which belongs in a verification plan.
Coordinating both verification and validation together in one document, which belongs in a combined V&V plan.
Recording actual observed validation outcomes, which belongs in a validation evidence record.
specifications.summary: Plan intended-use fitness validation scenarios, representative contexts, criteria, resources, and evidence
specifications.title: Validation plan
use_when: A project needs a dedicated plan for assessing whether a solution satisfies stakeholder needs in representative use conditions.
A validation lead is mapping stakeholder needs to scenarios, evaluation criteria, representative actors, and expected evidence.
A reviewer is verifying that every planned validation activity traces to a real stakeholder or intended-use need.

not_for: Assessing intended-use fitness against stakeholder needs in representative conditions, which belongs in a validation plan.
Coordinating both verification and validation in one combined program plan.
Recording actual conformance observations, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Plan technical conformance verification methods, requirement coverage, criteria, resources, and evidence
specifications.title: Verification plan
use_when: A project needs a dedicated plan for assessing technical conformity of an item against specified engineering requirements.
A verification lead is mapping technical obligations to inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration methods and expected evidence packages.
A reviewer is verifying coverage completeness, exclusion justifications, and readiness prerequisites before verification begins.

not_for: Detailed module, data structure, algorithm, or runtime implementation design, which belongs in software or system design descriptions.
Recording a single isolated technical choice and its alternatives, which belongs in an architecture decision record.
Stating testable system or software obligations, which belong in requirements specifications.
specifications.summary: Architecture drivers, viewpoints, views, major elements, cross-view consistency, and key tradeoffs
specifications.title: Architecture description
use_when: An architect needs to document cross-cutting structure, behavior, allocations, and tradeoffs across explicit stakeholder viewpoints.
A team is evaluating whether a proposed architecture satisfies its drivers and checking cross-view correspondence.
A reviewer is assessing architectural change impact without diving into low-level build-to or module implementation details.

not_for: Authorized business-level obligations and operating rules, which belong in a business requirements specification.
Stakeholder-visible system capabilities and operating concepts, which belong in stakeholder requirements or concepts of operations.
Comparing scored technical alternatives with sensitivity analysis, which belongs in a trade study report.
specifications.summary: Sourced business or mission problem, stakeholder perspectives, desired outcomes, and boundaries
specifications.title: Business or mission needs
use_when: A sponsor or analyst must establish a sourced business or mission problem and desired outcomes before committing to solution requirements.
A team is capturing stakeholder perspectives, effectiveness measures, and constraints to frame downstream option analysis.
A reviewer is checking whether a needs document separates problem framing from premature technical design choices.

not_for: Exploratory framing of a problem or opportunity before obligations exist, which belongs in a business or mission needs document.
Stakeholder-facing system outcomes or whole-system technical obligations, which belong in stakeholder or system requirements specifications.
Tracking cross-source requirement status without authoring statements, which belongs in a requirements registry.
specifications.summary: Assessable business obligations, operating rules, constraints, origins, and authorization states
specifications.title: Business requirements specification
use_when: Business or mission objectives must be translated into identifiable, assessable business-level obligations and operating rules.
An analyst is documenting business constraints, authorization states, priorities, and downstream interfaces for review.
A reviewer is checking whether proposed business obligations are clearly separated from authorized requirements and technical implementation choices.

not_for: Executable operator commands, preflight checks, and rollback sequences for live systems, which belong in an operational runbook.
Formal assessable system obligations and verification bases, which belong in stakeholder or system requirements specifications.
Sustained staffing, monitoring, and support scheduling for an active service, which belongs in an operations and support plan.
specifications.summary: Stakeholder-facing concept of intended system use, roles, modes, scenarios, and support
specifications.title: Concept of operations
use_when: Stakeholders and engineers need a shared conceptual account of how an envisioned system will operate across roles, modes, and scenarios.
An author is documenting intended human-system interactions, support concepts, and operational impacts before locking detailed requirements.
A reviewer is verifying that operational scenarios remain conceptual without drifting into low-level interface parameters or operator runbooks.

not_for: Study-wide sampling, ethics, and schedule planning, which belong in a user research and discovery plan.
Preserving raw responses collected during sessions, which belongs in an elicitation and source record.
Synthesizing interpreted study outcomes or advance participant consent notices, which belong in findings or participant information documents.
specifications.summary: Reusable questionnaire, interview, or observation prompts, routing, capture rules, and administration readiness
specifications.title: Elicitation instrument
use_when: A researcher or analyst needs a reusable questionnaire, interview guide, or observation guide with literal prompts and capture rules.
An author is defining response vocabularies, branching and skip logic, participant safeguards, and pilot or review readiness criteria.
A reviewer is checking whether collection items avoid leading wording and separate unpiloted drafts from administration-ready instruments.

not_for: Step-by-step live incident mitigation and rollback procedures for operators, which belong in operational runbooks or playbooks.
General module structure, data schemas, and algorithms across a software item, which belong in a software design description.
Prioritizing hypothetical failure modes by criticality ranking, which belongs in failure modes and effects analysis.
specifications.summary: Technical fault detection, propagation, disclosure, recovery, observability, and caller behavior contracts
specifications.title: Error handling specification
use_when: A system or software scope needs explicit contracts for fault detection, error propagation, disclosure limits, and recovery behavior.
An engineer is aligning callers, operators, and security reviewers on terminal failure outcomes and diagnostic observability.
A reviewer is verifying that error semantics satisfy stated reliability, security, and interface compatibility obligations.

not_for: Stating required boundary interactions before selecting a concrete realization, which belongs in an interface requirements document.
Indexing multiple interfaces and pointers to their controlling documents, which belongs in an interface registry.
Providing consumer-facing API or CLI syntax lookup without cross-party agreement authority, which belongs in a technical reference.
specifications.summary: Controlled physical, information, or behavioral interface parameters, compatibility rules, and cross-party agreement
specifications.title: Interface control document
use_when: Two or more parties need a shared, controlled specification of concrete physical, data, or behavioral interface parameters.
An interface engineer is governing version compatibility rules, endpoint ownership, and joint change effectivity across a boundary.
A reviewer is checking whether proposed interface realizations are cleanly distinguished from mutually agreed baselines.

not_for: Controlling agreed physical, protocol, or schema realization parameters across parties, which belongs in an interface control document.
Indexing interface identifiers, criticality, and owners across a program, which belongs in an interface registry.
Documenting whole-system functional behavior unrelated to boundary exchanges, which belongs in a system requirements specification.
specifications.summary: Assessable obligations, limits, side responsibilities, and assessment bases at identified boundaries
specifications.title: Interface requirements document
use_when: Internal or external system boundaries need an authoritative statement of required interactions, limits, and responsibilities before realization.
An engineer is documenting testable interface obligations, numerical conventions, and open boundary issues across participating sides.
A reviewer is verifying that interface obligations define what must hold at the boundary without prematurely locking unselected implementations.

not_for: Recording live prefixes, VLANs, and DNS assignments currently in force, which belong in a network allocation register.
Tracking active firewall, ACL, or zone enforcement rules, which belong in a network access rule register.
Documenting physical cable, patch panel, and port connections, which belongs in a cabling schedule.
specifications.summary: Intended enterprise or data-center network topology, segmentation, routing, addressing, wireless, and services
specifications.title: Network design description
use_when: An enterprise or data-center network requires a controlled design defining topology, segmentation, routing, addressing, and network services.
A network architect is specifying trust zones, wireless coverage design, and supporting infrastructure dependencies for implementation.
A reviewer is checking whether intended network design choices stay distinct from live operational assignments and open decisions.

not_for: Concise symbol, API, CLI flag, or schema lookup without task walkthroughs, which belongs in a technical lookup reference.
Hands-on pedagogical exercises with learner checkpoints and cleanup, which belong in a learning tutorial.
Internal service recovery commands for operators managing a specific deployment target, which belong in an operational runbook.
specifications.summary: Recipient-facing installation, configuration, usage tasks, expected results, and limits for a product
specifications.title: Product guide
use_when: A delivered product or tool needs recipient-facing instructions covering installation, configuration, everyday use, and recovery limits.
An author is writing a user manual or product operations guide aligned with actual delivered product behavior.
A reviewer is checking whether installation steps, settings, expected results, and boundaries reflect verified behavior without overclaiming.

not_for: Maintaining a cumulative multi-release history plus pending unreleased work, which belongs in a cumulative changelog.
Recording internal deployment actions, artifacts, and release authorization evidence, which belongs in a release record.
Communicating vulnerability applicability and remediation across affected versions, which belongs in a recipient security advisory.
specifications.summary: One-release recipient notice detailing changes, required actions, compatibility effects, and known limits
specifications.title: Release notes
use_when: A specific product or service release needs a concise notice informing recipients of changes, upgrade actions, compatibility, and limits.
A release coordinator is authoring user-facing upgrade instructions and breaking-change warnings for one release.
A reviewer is checking whether recipient-facing release notes expose required actions and unresolved limitations truthfully.

not_for: Comprehensive installation, configuration, and user task manuals for a delivered product, which belong in a product guide.
Exhaustive API, CLI, or configuration lookup tables, which belong in a technical lookup reference.
Detailed help-desk routing and security disclosure channels alone, which belong in a support and request-routing guide.
specifications.summary: Concise development repository entrypoint covering purpose, maturity, layout, setup, and documentation map
specifications.title: Repository overview
use_when: A development repository needs a clear top-level overview guiding users, contributors, and automated readers to authoritative resources.
A maintainer is documenting repository scope, maturity state, directory layout, setup examples, and support entrypoints.
A reviewer is checking whether a repository overview stays concise and avoids unsupported maturity claims or installation authorization.

not_for: Internal study design, recruitment logistics, and analysis schedules, which belong in a user research and discovery plan.
Exact interview questions or survey items, which belong in an elicitation instrument specification.
Recording collected responses or signed consent evidence, which belong in elicitation records or separate consent records.
specifications.summary: Advance plain-language study notice covering activities, recordings, data handling, contacts, and withdrawal
specifications.title: Research participant information
use_when: A study involving human participants requires clear advance information before individuals decide whether to participate.
A researcher is documenting recording choices, data handling, withdrawal limits, and reachable contacts in plain participant-facing language.
A reviewer is verifying that participant notices separate information supply and comprehension checks from signed consent records.

not_for: Test-specific instrumentation, simulators, fidelity tradeoffs, and reset rules, which belong in a test environment specification.
Enterprise network topology, routing, and wireless engineering, which belong in a network design description.
Operational governance companions wrapping versioned IaC code, which belong in a provisioning governance companion.
specifications.summary: Target state, dependencies, access rules, and readiness criteria for an enabling runtime environment
specifications.title: Runtime environment specification
use_when: A development, integration, staging, or production environment needs a controlled target specification of platform state and readiness criteria.
An environment owner is specifying required tooling, connectivity, access rules, data constraints, and readiness gates.
A reviewer is checking whether an environment specification distinguishes required target state from actual instance readiness observations.

not_for: Tracking internal vulnerability triage, engineering fixes, and case closure, which belongs in a vulnerability record.
Coordinating internal intake and escalation workflows, which belongs in a vulnerability response playbook.
Communicating general non-security feature changes for a release, which belongs in release notes.
specifications.summary: Recipient security notice covering affected/fixed versions, impact, severity assessments, and remediation
specifications.title: Recipient security advisory
use_when: A product security issue requires controlled recipient communication covering affected versions, impact, severity basis, and remediation.
A security coordinator is publishing or revising an advisory while keeping unknown applicability distinct from not-affected status.
A reviewer is checking whether independent severity assessments, disclosure authority, and optional native exports are accurately bound.

not_for: High-level cross-cutting architecture viewpoints and system-wide tradeoffs, which belong in an architecture description.
Whole-system realization spanning hardware, physical elements, and people, which belongs in a system design description.
Stating what the software must accomplish before design choices are made, which belongs in a software requirements specification.
specifications.summary: Detailed software component responsibilities, interfaces, data models, algorithms, runtime, and rationale
specifications.title: Software design description
use_when: Software designers and implementers need a detailed design covering modules, interfaces, data models, algorithms, and runtime configuration.
A team is translating allocated software requirements and architecture into concrete build-to component responsibilities.
A reviewer is verifying software design coverage, data ownership, rationale, and open issues before or during implementation.

not_for: Whole-system obligations prior to allocation across software, hardware, and people, which belong in a system requirements specification.
Implementation modules, classes, and internal algorithms, which belong in a software design description.
Stakeholder outcomes framed in user language prior to technical allocation, which belong in a stakeholder requirements specification.
specifications.summary: Traceable, assessable obligations and verification bases allocated to one software item
specifications.title: Software requirements specification
use_when: A bounded software item needs controlled, traceable, and assessable functional, interface, data, and quality obligations.
A software engineer or analyst is defining software requirements with verification conditions and explicit authorization states.
A reviewer is checking whether software requirements remain testable, traced to parent origins, and free of unjustified design lock-in.

not_for: Initial problem framing before requirements are structured, which belongs in a business or mission needs document.
Whole-system technical specifications or allocated software obligations, which belong in system or software requirements specifications.
Narrative operating scenarios and human-system concepts alone, which belong in a concept of operations.
specifications.summary: Stakeholder-visible system outcomes, use constraints, origins, and validation bases before technical allocation
specifications.title: Stakeholder requirements specification
use_when: Elicited stakeholder needs, scenarios, and success criteria must be consolidated into a controlled stakeholder-level requirement set.
An analyst is defining stakeholder-visible capabilities and use constraints that will govern downstream system requirements and validation.
A reviewer is verifying stakeholder agreement state and ensuring technical design constraints appear only when truly stakeholder-imposed.

not_for: Internal support team staffing, runbooks, or escalation procedures, which belong in operations plans or standard operating procedures.
Product installation, configuration, and usage tutorials, which belong in a product guide.
Publishing vulnerability applicability and fixes to recipients, which belongs in a recipient security advisory.
specifications.summary: Recipient-facing routing for help, defect, improvement, and security reports with intake expectations
specifications.title: Support and request-routing guide
use_when: A product, repository, or service needs a clear recipient-facing guide directing users to help, bug, feature, and security channels.
A maintainer is specifying intake information expectations, supported versions, and confidential reporting rules.
A reviewer is checking that a support guide avoids inventing unbacked response commitments or exposing sensitive report channels publicly.

not_for: High-level cross-cutting architecture viewpoints and tradeoffs alone, which belong in an architecture description.
Software-only component, data structure, and algorithm design, which belongs in a software design description.
Staged integration schedules and bring-up gates, which belong in an integration plan.
specifications.summary: Realizable whole-system or subsystem design covering elements, allocations, interfaces, behavior, and rationale
specifications.title: System design description
use_when: A whole system or subsystem requires a realizable design allocating obligations across hardware, software, human, and enabling elements.
A systems designer is specifying element responsibilities, resource rules, realization artifacts, and integration constraints at stated maturity.
A reviewer is checking whether a system design traces cleanly to allocated requirements without duplicating controlled interface masters.

not_for: Obligations allocated specifically to one software component, which belong in a software requirements specification.
Stakeholder outcomes stated in operational language prior to technical translation, which belong in a stakeholder requirements specification.
Detailed boundary protocols agreed across organizations, which belong in interface requirements or interface control documents.
specifications.summary: Assessable whole-system technical obligations, external interactions, qualities, constraints, and verification bases
specifications.title: System requirements specification
use_when: Stakeholder expectations or project decisions must be translated into controlled, assessable whole-system technical obligations.
A systems engineer is defining system behavior, performance, external interactions, and verification conditions prior to subsystem allocation.
A reviewer is checking whether system requirements avoid premature design lock-in and maintain complete traceability and authorization state.

not_for: Task-oriented installation and end-user workflows, which belong in a product guide.
Hands-on step-by-step exercises for learners, which belong in a learning tutorial.
Cross-party interface realization agreements, which belong in an interface control document.
specifications.summary: Version-bound technical lookup for APIs, SDKs, CLIs, protocols, settings, and schemas
specifications.title: Technical lookup reference
use_when: A product, library, CLI, or schema needs a version-bound lookup reference detailing exact syntax, types, defaults, errors, and limits.
An author is reconciling generated or hand-authored reference definitions against controlling source code or native schemas.
A reviewer is checking whether technical reference entries distinguish unknown defaults from zero or disabled values and bind real check status.

not_for: Campaign-level test strategy, schedules, and entry/exit gates, which belong in a test plan.
Deriving high-level test conditions and coverage techniques before concrete cases, which belongs in a test design specification.
Ordered multi-case operational run scripts or recorded actual run outcomes, which belong in test procedures or test execution records.
specifications.summary: Pre-execution test definitions with preconditions, inputs, stimuli, expected observations, and result criteria
specifications.title: Test case specification
use_when: One test or a coherent test case set needs a stable pre-execution specification of inputs, preconditions, actions, and pass/fail criteria.
A test designer is defining unambiguous expected observations and cleanup postconditions traced to requirements or risks.
A reviewer is checking whether test cases isolate individual assessable oracles without bloating into long shared execution scripts.

not_for: Simple inline scalar inputs belonging strictly to a single test case, which belong in a test case specification.
Configuring test hardware, simulators, and runtime instrumentation, which belongs in a test environment specification.
Recording actual test execution outcomes, which belongs in a test execution record.
specifications.summary: Reproducible test inputs, datasets, generation rules, provenance, protection, lifecycle, and suitability checks
specifications.title: Test data specification
use_when: Tests rely on shared, reproducible, sensitive, or generated datasets that require controlled definition beyond inline test-case values.
A test engineer or data steward is defining provenance, privacy protection, generation rules, and suitability checks for test inputs.
A reviewer is verifying that test datasets separate logical selection rules from materialized snapshot observations and expose coverage limits.

not_for: Campaign schedules, team assignments, and entry/exit gate governance, which belong in a test plan.
Concrete input values and exact per-case pass/fail oracles, which belong in a test case specification.
Step-by-step operator execution scripts and recovery branches, which belong in a test procedure.
specifications.summary: Derive test conditions, design techniques, planned cases, dependencies, and basis coverage
specifications.title: Test design specification
use_when: A bounded test basis needs explicit test conditions, justified design techniques, and planned case classes before authoring concrete cases.
A test designer is evaluating coverage completeness and surfacing data, environment, or sequencing dependencies early.
A reviewer is checking whether planned cases trace systematically to test conditions and stated risks.

not_for: General development, staging, or production enabling environments without test instrumentation, which belong in a runtime environment specification.
Defining reproducible input datasets and provenance rules, which belong in a test data specification.
Planning campaign-wide test strategy and schedules, which belongs in a test plan.
specifications.summary: Test environment configuration, fidelity, instrumentation, safety, readiness criteria, and restoration rules
specifications.title: Test environment specification
use_when: Test execution depends on a controlled hardware, software, or simulated environment with explicit instrumentation, fidelity, and reset rules.
A test engineer is defining readiness criteria and fidelity limits that govern which tests and conclusions an environment supports.
A reviewer is verifying that test environment requirements remain distinct from actual instance readiness observations.

not_for: Defining isolated test inputs and pass/fail oracles without shared sequencing, which belongs in a test case specification.
Broader multi-method technical conformance or stakeholder fitness procedures beyond test execution, which belong in verification or validation procedures.
Recording actual observations from an executed run, which belongs in a test execution record.
specifications.summary: Ordered test execution steps, setup checks, checkpoints, failure branches, evidence capture, and restoration
specifications.title: Test procedure
use_when: A test requires an explicit ordered execution script with setup checks, safety controls, failure branches, and restoration steps.
A test engineer or automation author is defining exact runtime checkpoints and evidence-capture rules for reproducible runs.
A reviewer is checking whether a test procedure bounds retries, protects shared assets, and restores clean end states.

not_for: Maintaining an internal inventory of component versions, origins, and licenses alone, which belongs in a software composition record.
Communicating user-facing feature changes or security vulnerabilities, which belong in release notes or security advisories.
Negotiating commercial intellectual-property terms in a contract, which belongs in a contracted engineering work agreement.
specifications.summary: Faithfully preserved upstream notices, attribution, and distribution obligations for a distributed artifact
specifications.title: Distributed third-party notices
use_when: A distributed software package or artifact includes third-party components carrying notice, copyright, or license-text attribution duties.
A release maintainer is assembling verbatim upstream notices and reconciling them against the exact distributed artifact.
A reviewer is verifying source traceability and unresolved notice gaps without fabricating redistribution rights or legal certification.

not_for: Comprehensive API, CLI, or setting lookup without guided exercises, which belongs in a technical lookup reference.
Production operational commands or maintenance procedures, which belong in an operational runbook.
General installation, configuration, and task documentation for end users, which belongs in a product guide.
specifications.summary: Safe, bounded hands-on learning exercise with prerequisites, checkpoints, reflection, cleanup, and walkthrough readiness
specifications.title: Learning tutorial
use_when: Learners need a safe, guided, hands-on practice exercise with clear prerequisites, observable checkpoints, recovery, and cleanup.
An author is distinguishing an untested tutorial draft from a verified learner-ready exercise backed by real walkthrough evidence.
A reviewer is verifying that tutorial commands target isolated environments, preserve unrelated work during cleanup, and never overclaim competence.

not_for: Assessing conformity to specified technical requirements via inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration, which belongs in a verification procedure.
Program-level validation strategy and resource scheduling, which belongs in a validation plan.
Recording actual observed validation outcomes and evidence, which belongs in a validation evidence record.
specifications.summary: Repeatable validation scenarios, representative contexts, actor roles, and intended-use fitness criteria
specifications.title: Validation procedure
use_when: A stakeholder, user, or mission need requires an executable validation scenario with representative actors and fitness criteria.
A validation designer is specifying scenario steps, safety prerequisites, expected observations, and result boundaries before running an event.
A reviewer is checking whether validation conclusions stay bounded to the needs and operating contexts the scenario can actually examine.

not_for: Assessing intended-use fitness against stakeholder needs in representative scenarios, which belongs in a validation procedure.
Detailed step-by-step operational test-runner scripts alone, which belong in a test procedure.
Recording actual conformance observations and verdicts, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Repeatable inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration method and technical conformance criteria
specifications.title: Verification procedure
use_when: Specific technical obligations require a repeatable inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration method with clear decision criteria.
A verification engineer is mapping requirements to measurement models, preconditions, ordered assessment steps, and evidence rules.
A reviewer is checking whether a verification method establishes clear conformance criteria before actual assessment runs.

not_for: Maintaining emergent, prioritized product backlog work items, which belong in an ordered product backlog.
Tracking live execution steps and recovery state for one bounded task session, which belongs in a task execution plan.
Tracking defects or nonconformances through root-cause analysis and disposition, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
specifications.summary: Track discrete follow-up actions with owners, status, due dates, dependencies, and closure evidence
specifications.title: Action item register
use_when: Discrete follow-up actions from reviews, audits, meetings, or operations require centralized ownership, due dates, and verified closure.
A coordinator is tracking blocked predecessors, overdue items, and unresolved owner assignments in one register.
A reviewer is confirming that closed actions cite checked closure evidence matching stated closure criteria.

not_for: Indexing status and pointers across many controlled decisions without full rationale, which belongs in a decision registry.
Quantitative multi-criteria option scoring with sensitivity analysis prior to choice, which belongs in a trade study report.
Formal acceptance or compliance signoff on a deliverable revision, which belongs in an approval and acceptance decision record.
specifications.summary: Record one architecture or technical choice with context, alternatives, rationale, state, and consequences
specifications.title: Architecture decision record
use_when: An architecture or technical decision requires a durable standalone record of context, alternatives, rationale, consequences, and status.
An architect or implementer needs to record decision authority, implementation follow-through, and explicit revisit conditions.
A reviewer is verifying whether a technical choice supersedes an earlier decision and exposes tradeoff consequences transparently.

not_for: Recording dated point-in-time technical observations from live scans, which belongs in an observed IT inventory.
Controlling baseline revisions and engineering changes across configuration items, which belongs in a configuration item register.
Tracking physical network cables and patch panels, which belongs in a cabling schedule.
specifications.summary: Governed IT asset identity, classification, ownership, custody, lifecycle state, and reconciliation
specifications.title: IT asset registry
use_when: An organization needs a governed registry tracking managed IT asset identities, classes, owners, custody, and lifecycle states.
An asset manager is reconciling authoritative asset records with configuration items, maintenance, financial, or retirement consumers.
A reviewer is checking whether governed asset custody and authority stay separate from raw discovery scans.

not_for: Tracking broader uncertain adverse events with likelihood and severity ratings, which belongs in a risk register.
Tracking discrete assigned follow-up tasks unrelated to validation of relied-upon assumptions, which belongs in an action item register.
Authoring formal approved system requirements, which belongs in requirements specifications.
specifications.summary: Control assumptions, dependencies, and constraints with owners, impact, validation, and escalation
specifications.title: Assumption and dependency register
use_when: Material assumptions, external dependencies, or constraints affect plans, architecture, schedules, or operations and require ongoing control.
A project lead or architect is assigning owners, validation actions, review timing, and failure impacts to relied-upon statements.
A reviewer is checking whether unvalidated assumptions or slipping dependencies trigger formal risk or change escalation.

not_for: Recording logical IP prefix, VLAN, and hostname assignments, which belongs in a network allocation register.
Designing logical network topology, routing, and security zones, which belongs in a network design description.
Tracking firewall or ACL traffic rules, which belongs in a network access rule register.
specifications.summary: Controlled schedule of planned or as-built cables, patch panels, ports, and endpoint connections
specifications.title: Cabling schedule
use_when: Network engineers, installers, or facility operators need a controlled schedule mapping cables, patch panels, ports, and endpoints.
An author is documenting planned or as-built physical cabling paths while exposing unverified connections or plant gaps.
A technician needs to determine exact panel-to-endpoint cabling connectivity at a stated as-of point.

not_for: Storing private keys, secret tokens, or credential material, which belong strictly in approved secret managers.
Tracking user accounts, system groups, and authorization privileges, which belongs in an identity and access register.
Executing step-by-step certificate rotation commands, which belongs in an operational runbook.
specifications.summary: Track certificate identity, scope, custodian, expiry, and installed locations while excluding private keys
specifications.title: Certificate register
use_when: A bounded set of services or hosts requires a controlled register of certificate identities, scopes, custodians, expiries, and locations.
Operators need reliable visibility into upcoming certificate renewals and where each certificate is installed.
A security reviewer is verifying that certificate metadata is tracked accurately without exposing private keys or secrets.

not_for: Requesting a temporary bounded departure while leaving the underlying obligation unchanged, which belongs in a deviation or waiver request.
Submitting an unapproved code diff for peer review in a repository, which belongs in a pull or merge request description.
Tracking a defect before a controlled baseline change is proposed, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
specifications.summary: Track proposed baseline change, impact, risk, rollback intent, authorization, implementation, and closure
specifications.title: Change request
use_when: A controlled product, service, configuration item, or baseline requires a formal proposal, impact assessment, and authorized change lifecycle.
A change coordinator is tracking authorization, implementation results, resulting baseline updates, and verified closure in one record.
A reviewer is checking whether rollback intent, impact analysis, and actual decision authority are complete before approval.

not_for: Writing a one-release upgrade notice focused solely on recipient actions, which belongs in release notes.
Preserving accountable deployment execution, artifacts, and channel evidence for one release, which belongs in a release record.
Authoring a repository entrypoint or setup overview, which belongs in a repository overview.
specifications.summary: Maintain meaningful multi-version change history and separated pending changes for one subject
specifications.title: Cumulative changelog
use_when: A project, product, or corpus maintains a cumulative version-by-version history plus pending unreleased changes.
A maintainer is categorizing notable additions, changes, removals, fixes, or exceptional release history across versions.
A reviewer is verifying that pending work stays clearly separated from established releases and avoids raw commit dumps.

not_for: Fixing one established multi-item snapshot for release or reproduction, which belongs in a configuration baseline record.
Tracking organizational custody and financial lifecycle of managed hardware or licenses, which belongs in an IT asset registry.
Recording point-in-time components observed by live discovery scans, which belongs in an observed IT inventory.
specifications.summary: Status accounting of candidate, controlled, and former configuration items, owners, revisions, and baselines
specifications.title: Configuration item register
use_when: A project or service needs centralized status accounting of candidate, controlled, and retained former configuration items.
A configuration manager is tracking item owners, authoritative locators, controlled revisions, parent hierarchies, and baseline links.
A reviewer is checking configuration discrepancies or verifying which revisions are currently under formal control.

not_for: Presenting an unaccepted offer, estimate, and quotation prior to agreement, which belongs in a technical and commercial proposal.
Planning internal technical execution or supplier oversight activities, which belong in project or supplier assurance plans.
Recording actual post-delivery acceptance signoff on an artifact revision, which belongs in an approval and acceptance record.
specifications.summary: Control parties, scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, commercial terms, and state of contracted engineering work
specifications.title: Contracted engineering work agreement
use_when: Established client and supplier parties need a structured control record of negotiated study, development, or maintenance commitments.
