A technical or commercial lead is aligning deliverables, receiving criteria, rights terms, and amendment precedence.
A reviewer is verifying that draft agreements remain distinct from executed commitments and reference real controlling sources.

not_for: Planning broader security engineering work and threat analysis across a lifecycle, which belongs in a security engineering plan.
Reporting findings from a completed formal audit examination, which belongs in an audit report.
Tracking individual discovered software vulnerabilities through patching, which belongs in a vulnerability record.
specifications.summary: Track selected security or compliance control implementation claims, parameters, status, evidence, and exceptions
specifications.title: Selected control implementation record
use_when: A project or system boundary must maintain per-control implementation claims, parameters, evidence links, and assessment status.
A security or compliance engineer is tracking planned, partial, implemented, inherited, and inapplicable controls transparently.
An assessor is verifying which evidence supports each control claim and which exceptions or limitations remain open.

not_for: Authoring full decision context, considered alternatives, rationale, and consequences, which belongs in an architecture decision record.
Recording formal authorization or acceptance signoff with authority evidence, which belongs in an approval and acceptance record.
Tracking open follow-up tasks generated by decisions, which belongs in an action item register.
specifications.summary: Unified status index of controlled decision masters, cited revisions, scope, supersession, and conflicts
specifications.title: Decision registry
use_when: Multiple controlled architecture, technical, or governance decisions need a unified searchable status index.
A registry steward is tracking decision supersession, affected scopes, review triggers, and conflicts across decision masters.
A reader needs to locate which decisions remain active without reading every individual decision master.

not_for: Permanently modifying a controlled baseline, requirement, or product configuration, which belongs in a change request.
Establishing organization-wide rules for when exceptions are permitted, which belongs in a policy or internal standard.
Tracking ongoing uncertain adverse events without a specific rule departure, which belongs in a risk register.
specifications.summary: Track a bounded deviation or waiver from an active obligation with impact, controls, authority, and closure
specifications.title: Deviation or waiver request
use_when: A team requests a temporary or item-scoped departure from an active requirement, baseline, or standard without modifying the rule itself.
A governance authority is evaluating impact, compensating controls, residual exposure, effectivity bounds, and closure conditions.
A reviewer is confirming that a requested departure stays visibly pending until an authorized grant or refusal is recorded.

not_for: Reporting active testing campaign progress and anomaly counts alone, which belongs in a test status report.
Reporting production service availability, telemetry coverage, and incidents, which belongs in a service-period status report.
Recording actual consumed hours for effort accounting, which belongs in an engineering effort and work-time record.
specifications.summary: Periodic engineering delivery status covering progress, resources, blockers, forecasts, and decision requests
specifications.title: Engineering delivery status report
use_when: An active engineering or software delivery effort needs a periodic status snapshot of progress, blockers, resources, and forecast.
A project or engineering lead is surfacing decision requests and replanning options grounded in sourced progress measures.
A reviewer is checking whether forecasts, assumptions, and actual progress remain separated cleanly.

not_for: Tracking system-level safety hazards and mishap acceptance across the lifecycle, which belongs in a hazard log.
Tracking broader project or operational business risks outside functional failure analysis, which belongs in a risk register.
Defining runtime software exception propagation and caller contracts, which belongs in an error handling specification.
specifications.summary: Analyze item or process failure modes, causes, effects, controls, priority, criticality, and treatments
specifications.title: Failure modes and effects analysis
use_when: Engineers need a systematic failure modes and effects analysis—or FMECA with criticality ranking—for a bounded item or process.
An analyst is prioritizing failure causes, existing controls, and treatment actions while exposing missing data and projected residual rankings.
A reviewer is checking whether rankings trace strictly to one declared method and distinguish projected outcomes from re-verified results.

not_for: Documenting version-bound software API symbols, CLI options, or schema fields, which belongs in a technical lookup reference.
Issuing mandatory engineering rules or compliance criteria, which belongs in an internal standard.
Recording architectural tradeoffs or formal requirements statements.
specifications.summary: Controlled concept-based vocabulary defining preferred terms, aliases, deprecated terms, origins, and distinctions
specifications.title: Concept-oriented glossary
use_when: A project or domain needs one controlled vocabulary unifying concept meanings, preferred terms, aliases, and deprecated labels.
A terminology steward is documenting definition origins, semantic distinctions, and unresolved term disputes across documents.
A reviewer is checking whether glossary entries define real underlying concepts rather than merely expanding acronyms.

not_for: Planning program-wide safety analyses, arguments, and lifecycle gates upfront, which belongs in a safety assurance plan.
Tracking non-safety project, cost, schedule, or operational risks, which belongs in a risk register.
Ranking functional component failure modes by engineering priority alone, which belongs in failure modes and effects analysis.
specifications.summary: Track system hazards, mishaps, safety controls, verification status, residual exposure, and acceptance
specifications.title: Hazard log
use_when: A safety-relevant system requires durable lifecycle tracking of hazards, mishaps, credited controls, verification, and residual exposure.
A safety analyst is exposing open hazards, unverified controls, and unaccepted residual safety exposure for review.
A safety authority is auditing closure evidence and control-to-verification traceability for each tracked hazard.

not_for: Storing credentials, keys, or secret tokens, which belong exclusively in approved secret stores.
Tracking public-key certificates and expiration dates, which belongs in a certificate register.
Tracking firewall or network ACL traffic rules, which belongs in a network access rule register.
specifications.summary: Controlled register of accounts, groups, privileges, and owners for a directory or host set
specifications.title: Identity and access register
use_when: A directory or bounded host set requires a controlled register of accounts, groups, assigned privileges, and owners.
An administrator or security reviewer is auditing who holds elevated privileges and surfacing unowned or unknown accounts.
A maintainer needs an as-of access inventory strictly free of passwords, tokens, or secret material.

not_for: Retrospective root-cause, dwell-time, control-failure, and lessons analysis after stabilization, which belongs in a cybersecurity post-incident review.
Non-cybersecurity service outages or operational disruptions, which belong in an operational incident record.
Managing unexploited software vulnerabilities, which belongs in a vulnerability record.
specifications.summary: Contemporaneous cybersecurity incident record covering detection, indicators, chronology, containment, eradication, and closure
specifications.title: Cybersecurity incident record
use_when: A suspected or confirmed cybersecurity incident is active and requires a contemporaneous factual record of detection, scope, and response.
An incident lead is tracking containment actions, eradication progress, indicators, notification duties, and evidence handling.
A responder or authority needs to decide whether a cybersecurity incident remains open or meets closure conditions.

not_for: Suspected or confirmed cybersecurity breaches involving indicators, eradication, or breach notifications, which belong in a cybersecurity incident record.
Post-stabilization root-cause and improvement analysis, which belongs in an operational post-incident review.
Tracking individual software bugs outside an active incident chronology, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
specifications.summary: Contemporaneous non-cybersecurity incident facts, chronology, impact, response, evidence, and closure
specifications.title: Operational incident record
use_when: A suspected or confirmed operational outage or non-cybersecurity disruption requires a contemporaneous timeline and status record.
An incident lead is tracking command handoffs, affected scope, containment, service restoration, and reclassification history.
Responders need a factual response record preserved cleanly for later retrospective review.

not_for: Stating detailed boundary obligations or controlled protocol parameters, which belong in interface requirements or interface control documents.
Mapping end-to-end bidirectional trace edges across requirements, design, and tests, which belongs in a requirements traceability matrix.
Documenting API syntax and CLI lookup tables for consumers, which belongs in a technical lookup reference.
specifications.summary: Controlled index of interface identities, parties, owners, criticality, status, and controlling definition links
specifications.title: Interface registry
use_when: A system or program with multiple internal and external interfaces needs one controlled index of interface identities and owners.
An interface steward is tracking registration status, criticality, known consumers, discrepancies, and pointers to controlling documents.
An engineer needs to locate which parties own an interface and where its authoritative specification resides.

not_for: Maintaining governed ownership, custody, and lifecycle authority for assets, which belongs in an IT asset registry.
Declaring desired baseline definitions or formal configuration releases, which belongs in configuration baseline or item records.
Listing embedded third-party software libraries inside one packaged release, which belongs in a software composition record.
specifications.summary: Dated observations of discovered IT components, attributes, collection limits, and baseline reconciliation
specifications.title: Observed IT inventory
use_when: Operations, security, or configuration teams need a dated factual account of IT components actually observed in a boundary.
An engineer is reconciling discovered host, software, or service attributes against governed asset registries or approved baselines.
A reviewer is examining collection coverage limits, unknown owners, or unreconciled inventory drift.

not_for: Designing overall network topology, segmentation architecture, and routing, which belongs in a network design description.
Tracking live IP prefixes, VLAN identifiers, and DNS names, which belongs in a network allocation register.
Recording firewall penetration-test or rule-verification outcomes, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Controlled register of ACL, firewall, and zone rules with enforcement boundary, owner, intent, and status
specifications.title: Network access rule register
use_when: A bounded network enforcement perimeter requires a controlled register of firewall, ACL, or zone rules with owners and intent.
Network or security reviewers need to determine which traffic rules are proposed, active, disabled, or superseded and why each exists.
An operator is surfacing unowned, ambiguous, or legacy access rules for cleanup.

not_for: Designing future network topology, routing architecture, and planned addressing, which belongs in a network design description.
Mapping physical cables, patch panels, and switch ports, which belongs in a cabling schedule.
Tracking firewall or ACL traffic permissions, which belongs in a network access rule register.
specifications.summary: Current in-force assignments of IP prefixes, VLAN IDs, network names, owners, and plan conflicts
specifications.title: Network allocation register
use_when: Network operators need an authoritative statement of IP prefixes, VLAN IDs, names, and owners currently assigned in force.
An engineer is detecting allocation conflicts between live network assignments and intended network design plans.
A team is tracking network address space cleanly without mixing unassigned proposals into active allocation rows.

not_for: Step-by-step troubleshooting commands and rollback procedures triggered by an alert, which belong in an operational runbook.
Reporting observed telemetry trends and service availability over a past window, which belongs in a service-period status report.
Defining overall operations staffing and support commitments, which belongs in an operations and support plan.
specifications.summary: Controlled catalog of watched signals, thresholds, owners, response routing, and monitoring gaps
specifications.title: Observability register
use_when: A service or system needs a controlled inventory of watched metrics, logs, probes, thresholds, owners, and expected responses.
An operator or reliability engineer is auditing monitoring coverage gaps and verifying every alert threshold has a real owner.
A team is standardizing watched operational signals separately from detailed remediation runbooks.

not_for: Tracking uncertain future events that have not occurred, which belongs in a risk register.
Tracking active operational or security outage chronologies, which belongs in an incident record.
Linking multiple test anomalies across runs to existing problem records, which belongs in a test anomaly reference.
specifications.summary: Control one observed defect or nonconformance through reproduction, analysis, disposition, verification, and closure
specifications.title: Problem or defect report
use_when: An observed software bug, hardware fault, or specification nonconformance requires structured analysis, disposition, and verified closure.
An engineer or quality lead is recording reproduction results, affected configurations, correction links, and effectiveness checks.
A reviewer is confirming that defect closure rests on real authority and verified correction rather than an untested patch.

not_for: Communicating high-level multi-horizon strategic themes and outcomes, which belongs in a product roadmap.
Authoring approved, traceable requirement statements, which belongs in requirements specifications.
Triaging raw customer feedback and discovery notes before product-work creation, which belongs in a product feedback register.
specifications.summary: Emergent ordered inventory of candidate product work, refinement basis, native states, and dependencies
specifications.title: Ordered product backlog
use_when: A product team needs an ordered, emergent inventory of candidate work items with explicit refinement states, sizing, and dependencies.
A product owner is documenting native board work states and optional normalized views without conflating selection with commitment.
A reviewer is checking whether backlog items preserve separate authoritative masters for requirements and formal delivery acceptance.

not_for: Prioritizing and refining selected product delivery work, which belongs in an ordered product backlog.
Reporting synthesized outcomes from a formal user research round, which belongs in user and context research findings.
Tracking confirmed defects through reproduction and closure, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
specifications.summary: Capture sourced product feedback and discovery inputs through triage, deduplication, and downstream routing
specifications.title: Discovery input and product feedback register
use_when: Ongoing user feedback, support observations, suggestions, or discovery notes need centralized intake and triage before formal work creation.
A product analyst is linking duplicates, grouping themes, and routing triaged items to requirements, backlogs, or defect records.
A reviewer is checking that raw feedback retains provenance and is never confused with approved commitments.

not_for: Preserving performed peer-review findings, severities, and formal review verdicts, which belongs in a code review record.
Governing formal cross-team baseline change approvals across systems, which belongs in a change request.
Recording actual release distribution or deployment outcomes, which belongs in a release record.
specifications.summary: Present one bounded diff for review with rationale, snapshot-bound checks, risks, rollout, and questions
specifications.title: Pull or merge request description
use_when: A change author is preparing or submitting a bounded repository diff for pull-request or merge-request review.
A reviewer needs concise rationale, concrete before-and-after results, actual snapshot-bound check evidence, and rollback limits.
A maintainer is checking whether host base/head changes invalidate prior check applicability before integration.

not_for: Authoring authoritative requirement wording, which belongs in business, stakeholder, system, software, or interface requirements specifications.
Mapping directed links from requirements to design, decisions, and tests, which belongs in a requirements traceability matrix.
Accounting for per-requirement verification methods and pass/fail coverage, which belongs in a requirements verification matrix.
specifications.summary: Cross-source index of requirement IDs, controlling sources, content states, owners, and reconciliation gaps
specifications.title: Requirements registry
use_when: Controlled requirements spread across multiple specifications need one unified index of IDs, sources, owners, and content states.
A requirements steward is reconciling duplicate IDs, orphaned entries, or conflicting requirement states across documents.
A reader needs to locate which authoritative specification owns a requirement without copying editable wording.

not_for: Tracking per-requirement verification methods, criteria, and conformance status, which belongs in a requirements verification matrix.
Tracking stakeholder need validation scenarios and fitness outcomes, which belongs in a validation matrix.
Indexing requirement IDs, owners, and content states alone, which belongs in a requirements registry.
specifications.summary: Bidirectional directed links and missing-relationship visibility across needs, requirements, design, and evidence
specifications.title: Requirements traceability matrix
use_when: A project needs bidirectional navigation across needs, requirements, design, decisions, verification activities, and evidence.
A change analyst or V&V lead is performing change-impact analysis and exposing missing or disputed traceability edges.
A reviewer is checking traceability completeness without duplicating endpoint requirement text or test verdicts.

not_for: Tracking stakeholder or mission need fitness scenarios, which belongs in a needs and intended-use validation matrix.
Recording detailed observations and artifact digests from one verification event, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
General multi-endpoint tracing across design and decisions, which belongs in a requirements traceability matrix.
specifications.summary: Requirement-by-requirement verification methods, criteria, evidence citations, and conformance coverage accounting
specifications.title: Requirements verification matrix
use_when: A bounded set of technical requirements requires a requirement-by-requirement verification planning and conformance coverage view.
A verification lead is tracking mapped methods, criteria, executed evidence links, and unverified facets across configurations.
A reviewer is identifying unresolved verification gaps before release or acceptance decisions.

not_for: Setting organization-wide mandatory risk criteria and escalation governance, which belongs in a risk management policy.
Tracking safety-critical physical or system hazards and mishaps, which belongs in a hazard log.
Tracking already occurred software defects or known maintainability compromises, which belong in defect or technical debt registers.
specifications.summary: Ongoing assessment, ownership, treatment, monitoring, and residual-exposure control for uncertain risks
specifications.title: Risk register
use_when: A project, product, or service needs ongoing tracking of uncertain adverse events, ratings, owners, treatments, and monitoring triggers.
A risk owner or manager is prioritizing exposure, escalating treatments, and reviewing open residual-risk acceptance decisions.
A reviewer is checking whether realized problems are kept distinct from uncertain future risks.

not_for: Reporting software or engineering project delivery milestones, which belongs in an engineering delivery status report.
Maintaining active alert definitions and thresholds, which belongs in an observability register.
Logging contemporaneous outage timelines or post-incident root-cause reviews, which belong in incident records or post-incident reviews.
specifications.summary: Periodic production service results, telemetry coverage limits, event summaries, trends, and follow-up requests
specifications.title: Service-period status report
use_when: An operating production service needs a periodic or as-of report summarizing observed metrics, telemetry coverage, incidents, and trends.
A service owner is requesting operational follow-ups grounded in measured period results and explicit data-coverage limits.
A reviewer is verifying that missing monitoring data is reported transparently rather than presented as healthy service operation.

not_for: Assembling verbatim upstream copyright notices and license texts for distribution, which belongs in distributed third-party notices.
Tracking live deployed servers and infrastructure hosts, which belongs in an observed IT inventory.
Recording formal vulnerability triage or security advisories, which belong in vulnerability records or security advisories.
specifications.summary: Controlled inventory of components, exact versions, origins, and licenses inside one software item
specifications.title: Software composition record
use_when: A specific software item and version requires a controlled inventory of contained components, exact versions, origins, and licenses.
A maintainer or security reviewer is checking component provenance and surfacing missing version or license metadata.
A team needs a factual composition record feeding vulnerability assessment or distribution notice assembly.

not_for: Project-wide engineering schedules, budgets, or multi-team release planning, which belong in development or systems engineering plans.
Serving as an authoritative master for organizational decisions, actions, or approvals, which belong in formal registers or evidence records.
Logging raw command transcripts or recording completed responsibility transfers between parties, which belong in handoff records.
specifications.summary: Living execution state of one bounded task covering steps, decisions, checks, blockers, and continuation
specifications.title: Task execution plan
use_when: A bounded multi-step task needs durable state tracking, recovery checkpoints, or cross-session handoff without an existing formal plan.
An operator or agent is recording completed versus deferred steps, decisions, executed verification checks, and concrete blockers.
A receiving agent needs to resume bounded work safely with clear authorization boundaries and release conditions.

not_for: Controlling mutually negotiated and executed contractual commitments, which belongs in a contracted engineering work agreement.
Organizing internal technical schedules and team staffing after award, which belongs in development or systems engineering plans.
Recording actual historical hours consumed, which belongs in an engineering effort and work-time record.
specifications.summary: Bounded engineering offer detailing scope, deliverables, estimates, quotation, proposed terms, and negotiation state
specifications.title: Technical and commercial proposal
use_when: An engineering team is preparing a bounded study, development, integration, or maintenance offer with deliverables and pricing.
A technical or commercial lead is documenting estimate assumptions, milestones, quotation lines, and offer response terms.
A reviewer is checking that an engineering proposal stays distinct from an executed contract or unilateral authorization.

not_for: Tracking uncertain adverse events that have not materialized, which belongs in a risk register.
Tracking broken functionality or specification nonconformances requiring defect closure, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
Prioritizing new customer-facing feature work, which belongs in an ordered product backlog.
specifications.summary: Track known engineering compromises, carrying effects, treatment options, disposition states, and reassessment
specifications.title: Technical debt register
use_when: Known engineering or architectural compromises create ongoing carrying costs that need transparent prioritization or deferred tracking.
An architect or maintainer is comparing treatment options, assigning owners, and recording revisit triggers for technical debt.
A reviewer is checking whether debt items cite observed carrying effects without fabricating dollar valuations or productivity claims.

not_for: Performing root-cause analysis and owning formal defect disposition, which belongs in a problem or defect report.
Logging complete step-by-step observations from one initiated test run, which belongs in a test execution record.
Reporting overall test campaign progress and schedule forecast, which belongs in a test status report.
specifications.summary: Linking view connecting test anomalies to runs, problem records, derived dispositions, constraints, and retests
specifications.title: Test anomaly reference
use_when: A test effort needs one unified view linking observed test anomalies to runs, problem records, testing constraints, and retests.
A test lead is tracking which anomalies block active testing or require retest while keeping dispositions anchored in problem masters.
A reviewer is reconciling test anomalies against closure evidence across multiple runs.

not_for: Summarizing an ended test campaign against formal exit criteria, which belongs in a test completion report.
Recording detailed case-by-case observations from one single run, which belongs in a test execution record.
Reporting broad engineering delivery progress beyond testing, which belongs in an engineering delivery status report.
specifications.summary: Periodic active-testing status covering progress, coverage, anomalies, blockers, risks, and labeled forecasts
specifications.title: Test status report
use_when: An active test campaign needs a periodic progress snapshot detailing execution counts, coverage, anomalies, blockers, and forecast.
A test lead is flagging active impediments and pending decisions required to keep testing on track.
A reviewer needs current testing status without confusing in-flight forecasts with campaign completion.

not_for: Recording an already authorized architecture choice and its follow-through, which belongs in an architecture decision record.
Investigating one technical question or model without comparing competing candidate options, which belongs in a technical analysis report.
Presenting a client quotation and commercial terms, which belongs in a technical and commercial proposal.
specifications.summary: Structured comparison of credible alternatives against gates, criteria, sensitivity, risks, and proposed recommendation
specifications.title: Trade study report
use_when: An engineering choice requires structured comparison of credible alternatives against mandatory gates, explicit criteria, uncertainty, and risk.
An analyst is performing sensitivity checks to verify whether a proposed recommendation stays robust before presenting to decision makers.
A reviewer is checking whether a trade study separates analytical recommendation from actual decision authorization.

not_for: Tracking technical requirement conformity via inspection, analysis, or test, which belongs in a requirements verification matrix.
Recording detailed per-event validation observations and artifact digests, which belongs in a validation evidence record.
Planning program-level validation schedules and resources before execution, which belongs in a validation plan.
specifications.summary: Map stakeholder or mission needs to validation scenarios, criteria, evidence, and current fitness outcomes
specifications.title: Needs and intended-use validation matrix
use_when: A bounded set of stakeholder, business, or mission needs requires a consolidated tracking view of validation scenarios and fitness outcomes.
A validation lead is monitoring which needs have credible validation paths and which remain uncovered, failed, or inconclusive.
A reviewer is checking whether intended-use fitness accounting cites real validation evidence under representative conditions.

not_for: Writing ordered step-by-step conformance execution instructions, which belongs in a verification procedure.
Tracking requirement-by-requirement verification status and evidence, which belongs in a requirements verification matrix.
Recording actual observed verification outcomes, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Controlled index of reusable verification methods, applicability, capability limits, states, and procedure links
specifications.title: Verification method register
use_when: A project uses multiple reusable verification methods or variants and needs one shared catalog of applicability and capability limits.
A verification planner is selecting authorized assessment methods and linking them to procedures and planned activities.
A reviewer is checking which proposed verification methods remain pending approval and what limitations bound their use.

not_for: Coordinating repeatable team workflows for vulnerability intake and triage, which belongs in a vulnerability response playbook.
Publishing affected product versions and fixes to external customers, which belongs in a recipient security advisory.
Logging active suspected or confirmed exploitation, which belongs in a cybersecurity incident record.
specifications.summary: Track one vulnerability case through applicability determination, treatment, verification, and closure
specifications.title: Vulnerability record
use_when: One discovered or reported vulnerability requires a controlled record of applicability, chosen treatment, verification, and closure state.
A vulnerability owner is linking an owned-code defect, tracking pending fixes, and recording verified remediation evidence.
A security authority is deciding whether a vulnerability case may close or remains open with explicit residual risk.

not_for: Recording technical architecture tradeoffs and design choices, which belong in an architecture decision record.
Indexing multiple decisions across a project without full decision authority records, which belongs in a decision registry.
Documenting technical review findings prior to separate formal acceptance, which belongs in a design review record.
specifications.summary: Authoritative record of one actual approval, acceptance, authorization, rejection, or withdrawal decision
specifications.title: Approval and acceptance decision record
use_when: An authorized person or governance body has made an approval, acceptance, authorization, rejection, or withdrawal decision requiring a durable record.
An author is binding a formal decision outcome, authority basis, conditions, and effectivity limits to an exact subject revision.
A reviewer is confirming whether a claimed signoff rests on real authority and evidence rather than a recommendation or delivery.

not_for: Peer examination of source code diffs, which belongs in a code review record.
Lifecycle design-gate evaluations such as preliminary or critical design reviews, which belong in design review records.
Evaluating technical requirements conformity for one build, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Performed audit record covering authorization, criteria, examined evidence, findings, limits, and conclusions
specifications.title: Audit report
use_when: An audit or formal assessment has been performed and requires a factual record of criteria, inspected evidence, findings, and bounded conclusions.
An auditor is documenting coverage limitations, finding classifications, and required follow-up references without overclaiming compliance.
A reviewer is checking whether every audit conclusion traces directly to inspected evidence within declared scope boundaries.

not_for: Submitting a proposed diff with rationale and pending reviewer questions prior to review, which belongs in a pull or merge request description.
Broad project or lifecycle design reviews beyond source inspection, which belong in technical review records.
Formal compliance audits against assurance baselines, which belong in an audit report.
specifications.summary: Performed review of an immutable source snapshot covering criteria, findings, dispositions, and outcome
specifications.title: Code review record
use_when: A code review has occurred and requires a durable record of the reviewed immutable snapshot, applied criteria, findings, and dispositions.
A reviewer is recording inspected automated checks, finding resolutions, re-review triggers, and outcome limits.
An auditor is confirming that a claimed code review actually inspected the exact revision under consideration.

not_for: Maintaining an ongoing catalog of candidate, controlled, and former items across baselines, which belongs in a configuration item register.
Recording an actual deployment or distribution attempt of a baseline, which belongs in a release record.
Recording components discovered in a live runtime scan, which belongs in an observed IT inventory.
specifications.summary: Established configuration snapshot fixing exact controlled item revisions, integrity, deviations, and effectivity
specifications.title: Configuration baseline record
use_when: A functional, allocated, product, software, infrastructure, operational, or document configuration has been formally baselined.
A configuration manager is fixing exact controlled item revisions, integrity bindings, active deviations, and effectivity for reproduction.
A reviewer is verifying what exact item set and constraints constitute an established baseline prior to change or release.

not_for: Earlier requirements or preliminary-design gates, which belong in SRR or PDR design review records.
Test or operational readiness gates, which belong in TRR or ORR design review records.
General non-standard technical peer reviews, which belong in a project-defined technical review record.
specifications.summary: Held Critical Design Review assessing detailed-design maturity for fabrication, integration, and test
specifications.title: Critical design review record
use_when: A Critical Design Review has been held and requires an authoritative record of entrance results, detailed-design maturity assessment, and disposition.
A review chair is documenting CDR findings, action items, constraints, and conditional go-ahead rules for fabrication and integration.
A stakeholder is inspecting exact reviewed design editions and conditions decided at a held CDR gate.

not_for: Formal milestone reviews such as SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, or ORR, which have dedicated design review specifications.
Inspecting immutable source code diffs, which belongs in a code review record.
Ordinary coordination meetings without formal assessment criteria, which belong in an engineering meeting record.
specifications.summary: Held project-defined technical or peer review covering criteria, examined evidence, findings, and disposition
specifications.title: Project-defined technical review record
use_when: A project-defined technical, design, or lifecycle peer review has been held under custom review questions and criteria.
A review chair is recording examined subject editions, criterion assessments, findings, follow-up actions, and board disposition.
A reviewer is checking whether a custom technical review preserves actual evidence and clear conditional proceed or repeat decisions.

not_for: Pre-test readiness reviews for test articles and facilities, which belong in a Test Readiness Review record.
Earlier requirements or design maturity reviews such as SRR, PDR, or CDR.
Planning future cutover and handover stages before deployment, which belongs in a transition and deployment plan.
specifications.summary: Held Operational Readiness Review evaluating deployed system and support-organization readiness
specifications.title: Operational readiness review record
use_when: An Operational Readiness Review has been held and requires a record of deployed-state readiness, support elements, findings, and disposition.
A review chair is documenting operational readiness criteria, residual risks, open conditions, and transition go-ahead decisions.
An operations leader is inspecting evidence supporting whether a deployed system and support organization were judged ready.

not_for: Earlier requirements credibility reviews, which belong in a System Requirements Review record.
Later detailed-design maturity reviews for fabrication and integration, which belong in a Critical Design Review record.
Authoring the system or software design content itself, which belongs in design description specifications.
specifications.summary: Held Preliminary Design Review assessing preliminary design adequacy as a basis for detailed design
specifications.title: Preliminary design review record
use_when: A Preliminary Design Review has been held and requires a record of design-basis assessment, entrance results, findings, and disposition.
A review chair is binding PDR conditions, actions, and proceed decisions to exact preliminary-design and requirement editions.
A reviewer is verifying whether a preliminary design passed gate criteria before entering detailed design.

not_for: Preliminary or detailed design maturity reviews, which belong in PDR or CDR design review records.
Authoring the system requirements statements themselves, which belongs in a system requirements specification.
Recording formal requirement baseline signoff alone, which belongs in an approval and acceptance decision record.
specifications.summary: Held System Requirements Review assessing requirements credibility and readiness to proceed
specifications.title: System requirements review record
use_when: A System Requirements Review has been held and requires a record of requirements credibility assessment, findings, actions, and disposition.
A review chair is binding SRR entrance results and proceed conditions to exact examined requirement editions.
A stakeholder is verifying whether system requirements were judged credible enough to proceed into preliminary design.

not_for: Operational deployment readiness after testing, which belongs in an Operational Readiness Review record.
Planning test objectives, schedules, and entry criteria prior to the review, which belongs in a test plan.
Recording observations during actual test runs, which belongs in a test execution record.
specifications.summary: Held Test Readiness Review evaluating test article, environment, personnel, procedures, and data controls
specifications.title: Test readiness review record
use_when: A Test Readiness Review has been held for a bounded test or test series and requires an authoritative readiness record.
A review chair is recording article configuration, procedure and facility readiness, safety issues, findings, and disposition.
A test lead is verifying exact reviewed editions and conditions established before test execution begins.

not_for: Designing interview prompts or questionnaires before collection, which belongs in an elicitation instrument specification.
Presenting interpreted themes, patterns, and product implications, which belongs in user and context research findings.
Recording ordinary project coordination meetings, which belongs in an engineering meeting record.
specifications.summary: Preserve raw elicitation statements, observations, provenance, custody, and capture gaps before interpretation
specifications.title: Elicitation and source record
use_when: An interview, workshop, survey, observation, or source-acquisition session has started and raw outputs must be preserved before interpretation.
A researcher or analyst is documenting raw statements, applied instruments, permission provenance, redactions, and capture gaps.
A reviewer is tracing synthesized findings or requirements back to unedited raw collection records and custody rules.

not_for: Reporting delivery progress, impediments, and schedule forecasts, which belongs in an engineering delivery status report.
Estimating future effort or pricing for a client offer, which belongs in a technical and commercial proposal.
Recording technical work performed on an operational target, which belongs in an operational work execution record.
specifications.summary: Preserve actual consumed engineering effort, units, attribution, totals, corrections, and use limits
specifications.title: Engineering effort and work-time record
use_when: An engineering activity has consumed effort that requires a proportionate, auditable record of actual time, units, and attribution.
A coordinator or performer is reconciling effort totals, recording corrections, and stating counting rules for authorized accounting.
A reviewer is checking that effort actuals stay distinct from completion claims, remaining estimates, or productivity judgments.

not_for: Planning future cutover and operational entry stages before transfer begins, which belongs in a transition and deployment plan.
Recording software or artifact publication to channels, which belongs in a release record.
Tracking ongoing task state for a single worker or session continuation, which belongs in a task execution plan.
specifications.summary: Record actual transfer of responsibility, custody, items, access, receipt, open items, and response
specifications.title: Handoff and transfer record
use_when: A bounded transfer of operational ownership, custody, access, deliverables, or knowledge has begun between identified parties.
A delivering or receiving owner is recording transferred baselines, open obligations, receipt evidence, and formal receiving responses.
A reviewer is checking who currently holds responsibility and which conditions remain unresolved before handoff closure.

not_for: Retrospective root-cause and response reviews of stabilized operational or cybersecurity incidents, which belong in post-incident reviews.
Issuing binding process updates or reusable advisory conventions directly, which belong in policies, standards, or engineering guides.
Tracking discrete assigned follow-up tasks across sources, which belongs in an action item register.
specifications.summary: Evidence-based lessons, bounded interpretations, recommendations, and improvement actions from non-incident work
specifications.title: Lessons learned record
use_when: Non-incident project, engineering, delivery, or maintenance work produced evidence-based insights worth preserving for future teams.
A team is documenting factual observations, applicability bounds, proposed improvements, and target knowledge destinations.
A reviewer is checking whether lessons stay grounded in actual evidence and distinguish proposed changes from adopted standards.

not_for: Formal criteria-based design or peer reviews, which belong in design review or project-defined technical review records.
Authoritative architectural choices or formal approvals, which belong in architecture decision or approval records.
Preserving raw user research interviews or observations, which belongs in an elicitation and source record.
specifications.summary: Record held ordinary meeting subjects, factual discussion, decisions, open questions, and assigned follow-up
specifications.title: Engineering meeting record
use_when: An ordinary engineering or project coordination meeting took place and its discussion, open questions, and follow-ups must be preserved.
A facilitator is capturing factual session outcomes and corrections without conflating meeting notes with formal approvals.
A participant needs an accurate record of what was discussed and assigned during a held coordination session.

not_for: Authoring repeatable operational instructions before work starts, which belongs in an operational runbook or work instruction.
Recording executed test runs and test-case verdicts, which belongs in a test execution record.
Recording product release distribution across channels, which belongs in a release record.
specifications.summary: Evidence of operational or maintenance work covering authority, method, as-found/as-left state, and outcome
specifications.title: Operational work execution record
use_when: Operational or maintenance work on a live system or asset has started and requires durable evidence of actions and resulting state.
An operator or maintainer is recording as-found state, method deviations, observed outcomes, and return-to-service disposition.
An investigator needs a truthful account of a completed, aborted, failed, or unauthorized operational attempt.

not_for: Contemporaneous logging during an active cybersecurity incident, which belongs in a cybersecurity incident record.
Retrospective reviews of non-security operational outages, which belong in an operational post-incident review.
Retaining lessons from routine non-incident engineering projects, which belongs in a lessons learned record.
specifications.summary: Retrospective cybersecurity incident review covering causes, controls, dwell time, eradication, and improvements
specifications.title: Cybersecurity post-incident review
use_when: A cybersecurity incident has stabilized and teams have performed retrospective causal, control, dwell-time, and eradication analysis.
A security responder is documenting supported security control failures, notification assessment, and justified remediation actions.
A reviewer is checking whether retrospective cybersecurity findings stay bounded by inspected evidence and state open uncertainties.

not_for: Contemporaneous event chronologies and live response status, which belong in an operational incident record.
Retrospective analysis of cybersecurity incidents involving dwell time or eradication, which belongs in a cybersecurity post-incident review.
Non-incident project retrospectives, which belong in a lessons learned record.
specifications.summary: Retrospective operational incident review covering causes, response effectiveness, lessons, and improvements
specifications.title: Operational post-incident review
use_when: A non-cybersecurity operational incident has stabilized and a retrospective analysis of causes, response, and recovery has been performed.
A service owner is capturing contributing conditions, recovery effectiveness, and concrete improvement actions backed by evidence.
A reviewer is confirming that causal findings reflect inspected evidence and distinguish supported conclusions from speculation.

not_for: Communicating user-facing changes and upgrade instructions to recipients, which belongs in release notes.
Maintaining a cumulative version history across multiple releases, which belongs in a cumulative changelog.
Defining a controlled item snapshot without recording distribution actions, which belongs in a configuration baseline record.
specifications.summary: Accountable record of one begun release event covering configuration, authority, actions, and outcome
specifications.title: Release record
use_when: A software, system, or documentation release attempt has started or completed and requires an accountable factual record.
A release manager is documenting exact released artifacts, baseline links, authorization evidence, channel outcomes, and restrictions.
An auditor or operator needs to determine precisely what configuration was made available and whether any interruption occurred.

not_for: Structured multi-criteria comparison of competing options against gates to select a choice, which belongs in a trade study report.
Recording technical requirement conformance verdicts, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
Recording an authorized choice and its architecture rationale, which belongs in an architecture decision record.
specifications.summary: Performed technical analysis preserving question, inputs, method, results, uncertainty, limits, and conclusions
specifications.title: Technical analysis report
use_when: Technical investigation, modeling, benchmarking, or root-cause analysis has started or completed and requires a reproducible report.
An analyst is documenting inputs, assumptions, methods, observed results, uncertainty, limitations, and proposed recommendations.
A reviewer is assessing whether analytical conclusions stay within what the performed work and data actually support.

not_for: Reporting periodic mid-campaign progress and forecasts while testing is still active, which belongs in a test status report.
Recording detailed per-case observations from one single test run, which belongs in a test execution record.
Planning test scope and exit criteria before testing begins, which belongs in a test plan.
specifications.summary: Ended test campaign summary reconciling runs, coverage, anomalies, exit-criteria assessment, and unresolved work
specifications.title: Test completion report
use_when: A bounded test campaign or phase has ended and requires a reconciled summary against adopted exit criteria.
A test lead is aggregating run outcomes, anomalies, coverage gaps, residual risks, and recommendations for stakeholders.
A reviewer is evaluating whether campaign exit criteria were satisfied or which unmet criteria require further testing.

not_for: Summarizing multiple runs at the end of an entire campaign, which belongs in a test completion report.
Defining expected inputs and test steps prior to execution, which belongs in test case or test procedure specifications.
Binding multi-method conformance observations to technical requirements overall, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
specifications.summary: Factual log of one initiated test run covering configuration, attempts, observations, and outcomes
specifications.title: Test execution record
use_when: A test run has been initiated and requires an exact factual log of tested configuration, attempted cases, observations, and outcomes.
A test operator is recording distinct retry attempts, aborted runs, unattempted selected cases, and anomaly links.
An investigator or test lead is reconstructing a specific run to judge pass/fail verdicts and determine retest needs.

not_for: Planning recruitment, methods, and ethics before conducting research, which belongs in a user research and discovery plan.
Preserving unedited raw statements and session transcripts, which belongs in an elicitation and source record.
Judging intended-use fitness of a delivered solution against fixed needs, which belongs in a validation evidence record.
specifications.summary: Supported discovery observations, themes, disagreements, confidence limits, and implications from performed research
specifications.title: User and context research findings
use_when: An exploratory user research round has collected observations or ended with capture limits that must be synthesized for decision makers.
A researcher is reporting grounded themes, participant disagreements, sample limitations, and implications for needs or product work.
A reviewer is checking whether discovery insights trace to real collection records and preserve confidence and scope boundaries.

not_for: Recording technical conformity against specified engineering requirements, which belongs in a verification evidence record.
Mapping program-wide needs to planned validation activities and aggregate status, which belongs in a validation matrix.
Designing validation scenarios prior to execution, which belongs in a validation plan or validation procedure.
specifications.summary: Observed intended-use fitness evidence bound to needs, assessed context, comparisons, and coverage limits
specifications.title: Validation evidence record
use_when: A validation activity has acquired observations—or closed an assessed scope with none—that must be bound to stakeholder needs.
A validation lead is recording assessed contexts, criteria comparisons, artifact digests, and demonstrated versus undemonstrated fitness facets.
A reviewer is checking whether intended-use fitness claims rest on real observations rather than planned scenarios.

not_for: Recording stakeholder intended-use fitness in representative scenarios, which belongs in a validation evidence record.
Logging low-level step-by-step execution of a single test run alone, which belongs in a test execution record.
Tracking requirement-by-requirement verification planning and summary coverage across a program, which belongs in a requirements verification matrix.
specifications.summary: Observed technical conformance evidence bound to requirements, assessed configuration, comparisons, and limits
specifications.title: Verification evidence record
use_when: A verification activity has acquired conformance observations—or closed an assessed scope with none—requiring binding to technical requirements.
A verification lead is recording assessed configurations, observed comparisons, artifact integrity, failed attempts, and retests.
A reviewer is auditing whether a technical pass claim names the exact requirement, criterion, actual configuration, and observation.
